content.title: Energy Governance for a Just Energy Transition

content.text: This module introduces the core principles, structures, and tools of energy governance essential for driving a <ai prompt="What is just energy transition?">just energy transition 💬️</ai>. It begins by introducing the fundamentals of energy governance, what it is, why it matters, and how it intersects with the principles of effectiveness, accountability, and inclusiveness. It explains the evolution from state-centered control to more distributed, multi-actor governance systems and introduces learners to key actors across sectors: governments, private industry, civil society, international organizations, and local communities. Building on this foundation, the module explores what constitutes good governance in energy transitions. It discusses how to design effective policy and regulatory frameworks, such as those that are coherent, adaptive, context-specific, and evidence-based. It also highlights the importance of transparency and regular oversight to ensure accountability and public trust. Learners are introduced to tools like Institutional and Context Analysis (ICA), Regulatory Impact Assessments (RIA), and data-driven policymaking to enhance governance performance. The module also utilizes case studies to illustrating governance challenges and solutions.The third chapter explores concrete policy and regulatory instruments. It introduces a typology of sustainable energy policy tools such as command and control and market based instruments.

objectives.title: Understand what energy governance is and how it can act as an enabler in achieving energy access and accelerating a just energy transition
Identify and describe the four focus areas of Energy Governance along with some examples and recommendations
